newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO SET UP PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT COMPANY - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO SET UP PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT COMPANY - MINISTER.

text.p: The Greek finance ministry will set up a portfolio management company that will manage the state's shares in part-floated and other listed companies, said deputy Finance Minister Nickos Christodoulakis.
The new company will have an initial equity of 50 million drachmas and will be fully-owned by the state, Christodoulakis told reporters.

It will carry out government orders regarding the management of shares of part-floated firms and shares of other listed companies such as National Bank if a decision is taken to convert bonds into shares, he said.
The draft law will be in parliament soon and is expected to be passed in July, he added.
"The company will add flexibility to portfolio management of shares and will be responsible for the allocation of proceeds from the part-flotation of state companies," he said.
High-level officials from the finance ministry will serve on the board of the new company, he said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
